blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: RIPA 2000 — Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000, historically specified by OCR.
IPA 2016 — Investigatory Powers Act 2016, governing major modern powers.
necessity — Intrusive step is needed for a legitimate legal aim.
proportionality — Intrusion is proportionate to the objective and circumstances.

blocks.title: OCR historic reference
blocks.text: RIPA 2000 sets out specified investigatory powers and safeguards; provisions have changed over time.

blocks.title: Current landscape
blocks.text: Investigatory Powers Act 2016 and later changes govern major communications powers and oversight.

blocks.title: Weigh safeguards
blocks.text: Intrusion should be assessed against lawful authority, necessity, proportionality and oversight. A different OCR requirement, 1.5.2 , considers broader ethical choices: a legally permitted technology can still introduce censorship, biased decisions, intrusive monitoring or avoidable environmental harm.

blocks.text: No. School monitoring has its own employment, safeguarding, privacy and policy considerations and must be lawful, transparent and proportionate as appropriate. Do not claim all ordinary IT logging requires a state-interception warrant.
